name: Alphaeus
overview: Alphaeus is a male figure mentioned in the New Testament, identified primarily as the father of James the disciple. Beyond this familial connection, Scripture does not provide further details about his tribe, surname, or additional attributes. His mention highlights his role within the early Christian community through his son.
namesAndTitles: The name Alphaeus appears as a proper name without a specified meaning in the biblical text. There is no indication that the name was given by God, and no further titles or meanings are associated with it in the provided reference.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Alphaeus as the father of James, one of Jesus' disciples. No other family relationships are documented beyond this connection in the provided information.
scriptureSignificance: Alphaeus is significant in the biblical narrative primarily due to his relationship to James, one of the twelve disciples of Christ. His mention in Matthew 10:3 situates him within the circle of those closely connected to Jesus' ministry. While Alphaeus himself does not have an active role recorded in Scripture, his identity as the father of a disciple underscores the human and relational dimension of the early Church.
